change: Move only BoxData into private reusable 64-entry Table COW pages; compact node cells retain opaque affine box-slot owners. Node/payload directories and free heads clone and restore together. No dependencies or per-box heap/RC.

build.profile: ordinary default-feature cargo build --release --lib --bin umber; workspace fat LTO, codegen-units=1, debug=1; no extra RUSTFLAGS

methodology.ordinary_cpu: One warmup plus seven measured sequential rotating baseline/prototype/native complete CLI samples per fixed book/mixed input, pinned CPU 3. Includes startup/source/font I/O, execution/layout, detached output construction/retention and teardown. Umber does not scan placements in the CLI; native INITEX writes DVI/log. Native-only hbadness/vbadness=10000. Existing fixed input files reused without regeneration.
methodology.heap: Separate external counting allocator measures engine construction/execution with preloaded host source/font buffers excluded. Requested/live bytes exclude allocator rounding/headers, stack and OS mappings. Fresh outcome adapter retains one Outcome, drops Engine, then drops Outcome. Retained adapter captures 60 book checkpoints plus outcomes every 10 paragraphs and validates exact suffix replay. Normal heap adapters contain no source instrumentation. Allocation comparison records use indexed Pages::get(index) lookup and fully reconstruct and compare both placement streams on demand inside the measured interval, excluding Pages::iter's separate temporary chunk-directory allocation.
methodology.physical: Independent instrumented source copies count allocated node chunks and private BoxSlot table pages, including cached backing, at phase boundaries. They are excluded from ordinary CPU and total-heap reports. Payload slots 48 B, payload page request 3,088 B including Rc header. Node chunks keep identical allocation/COW counts across versions. Separate directory/free-slot high-water costs are included in total heap.
methodology.replay_cpu: Three serial alternating invocations per version on CPU 3. Each runs 200 capture/restore operations and six suffix executions per 60/300/540 paragraph prefix; first suffix per invocation discarded. Capture/restore are wall-clock batch means; suffix execution/publication/comparison use separate wall-clock phases.15 retained suffix samples per prefix/version; shared-host measurements.

tradeoffs: Box-bearing node plus payload uses 72 B versus 56 B before page slack; nonbox nodes shrink 56 -> 24 B.

Payload Table retains its peak slot range and COW copies 64 headers per touched shared page. Fresh book/mixed each retain 2 payload pages at completion. 60 retained book roots use 91 physical payload pages including 89 COW pages.
Checkpoint capture increases~0.1–0.2us and restore~0.13–0.36us across measured prefixes. Suffix execution improves~2.3–3.2%.
Fresh complete heap improves 3.85% book and 2.66% mixed; retained 60 root book heap improves 35.18%. Existing Outcome-only totals are unchanged.
Warm suffix execution/publication still request 6 backing allocations. Payload pages reuse after the first replay, while the existing one-fresh-node-chunk-per-replay behavior remains.
Short shared-host measurements and different native output endpoints do not establish broad TeX/LaTeX or backend performance.

validation.native_oracles: All three explicitly invoked upstream font/paragraph/page adapters passed with pdfTeX 1.40.25 and the existing real TFM corpus.
validation.fixed_outputs: Complete counts/messages/boxes/fonts/font bytes/placements match baseline for both fixed cases. Retained checkpoint suffix outputs match. Independent native DVI placements match both cases.
validation.miri: All 10 nodes ownership/reuse/capacity/nested-release tests passed nightly Miri with -Zmiri-strict-provenance.
validation.checks: rustfmt check, git diff --check, all-target Clippy with -D warnings, ordinary release CLI/library/examples and wasm32-unknown-unknown library build passed.
validation.independent_review: Read-only reviewer found no actionable correctness issues in ownership/COW clone contexts, constructor order, node allocation search/addresses, generic BoxId rejection or release sequencing.
